title: Opposite Day
topic: Equations with variables on both sides

scenes.sub: Instant Replay: x on both sides
scenes.say: Math Blitz, day three! Instant Replay time. Yesterday's brawl got sneaky, so we're running it back with a secret weapon: Opposite Day!

scenes.heading: THE SECRET WEAPON
scenes.note: To cancel a term, do its OPPOSITE.
scenes.say: Here's the rule. To make a term vanish, do its opposite to both sides. Plus two x? Subtract two x. Minus four? Add four.

scenes.heading: MOVE 1: CANCEL THE 2x
scenes.say: Six x plus five equals two x plus seventeen. Plus two x? Subtract it from both sides! Now four x plus five equals seventeen.

scenes.heading: MOVE 2: FINISH IT
scenes.say: Opposite again! Subtract five: four x equals twelve. Divide by four: x equals three. Check it: both sides make twenty three. Nothing but net!

scenes.ask: What is the value of x?
scenes.say: Your turn, champ! Twenty five XP on the line. Seven x minus four equals three x plus sixteen. Remember Opposite Day! What is x? Tap your answer below the video!

question.prompt: 7x − 4 = 3x + 16. What is the value of x?
question.explain: Subtract 3x from both sides: 4x − 4 = 16. Add 4: 4x = 20, so x = 5. Check: 7(5) − 4 = 31 and 3(5) + 16 = 31.

trap_notes.2: Stopped at 4x = 20 and forgot to divide by 4
